adjudicated.jp: どんな犯罪に手を染めても、誰も咎めることもなく、また咎められることもない。
adjudicated.en:
no matter what crime one has had stained their
hands with, if no one rebukes you, then there
will be no being rebuked at all.
comments: Very careful here, he does not say that a world without people to call things crimes there'd be no crime. He says that without anyone to call on crimes, there'd be nothing CALLED a crime. Remember how he decides he is still stealing from the kouban. Consider Misato vs. her father: there's a higher law than the one of men, that won't pass or miss anything even if the law of men does. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The source imagines that no matter what crime he commits, nobody would condemn it and he could not be condemned. The English shifts between “one,” “their,” and “you” and reduces the second relation to a tautology.
adjudicated.remedy: Use “No matter what crime I committed, no one would condemn it, and there would be no one to condemn me.”

adjudicated.en:
If a person becomes Alone, the very essence of
this person alters.
adjudicated.assessment: The source says people necessarily change when alone. “Becomes Alone” needlessly capitalizes an adjective, and “this person” awkwardly repeats the subject.
adjudicated.remedy: Use “When a person is alone, they change.”

adjudicated.jp: 突き上げるような負の感情も、マイナスではなくなる。
adjudicated.en:
The negative emotions that try to swell out of
themselves stop being a minus point.
adjudicated.assessment: The source describes surging negative emotions ceasing to count as negative. “Swell out of themselves” is malformed, and “minus point” leaves the evaluative transformation opaque.
adjudicated.remedy: Use “Even the negative emotions surging up within a person would no longer be negative.”

highlights.text:
The negative emotions that try to swell out of
themselves stop being a minus point.

adjudicated.jp: 罪も罪でない世界なら。
adjudicated.en:
It would be a society, a world, where a sin is
not a sin.
adjudicated.assessment: The source is a conditional fragment leading into the next revelation. GHS preserves the broad content but regularizes it and redundantly adds society, a world.
adjudicated.remedy: Keep the conditional linkage without redundant world language.

highlights.text:
It would be a society, a world, where a sin is
not a sin.

adjudicated.jp: この『目』は、そのためにあったのだと、天啓のように思った。
adjudicated.en:
These 『eyes』 we have exist for that purpose, I
thought as if by divine revelation.
comments: He means more than just his Mystic Eyes. Or rather, it's the opposite. And in the end, Divine Revelation. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The source refers to the narrator’s singular marked “eye” as existing for that purpose. “These eyes we have” changes number and generalizes the eye to an inclusive group.
adjudicated.remedy: Use “I felt, like a revelation, that this ‘eye’ existed for that purpose.”

highlights.text:
These 『eyes』 we have exist for that purpose, I
thought as if by divine revelation.

adjudicated.jp: 「どうかしてる」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "You've gone mad."
comments: This is what Kiri will often tell him and her. -GHS

adjudicated.remedy: Optional idiomatic revision; no confirmed source-bound correction is established.

adjudicated.jp: 吐き捨てて、学校方面に歩き出す。
adjudicated.en: That I spit out, then go to walk towards the school.
adjudicated.assessment: The source says he spits the words out and starts walking toward school. “Go to walk towards” is unidiomatic.
adjudicated.remedy: Use “I spat the words out and started walking toward school.”

adjudicated.jp: いちいち構っていられない。
adjudicated.en: I don't need someone to worry about every single thing.
adjudicated.assessment: The source says he cannot stop to engage with every little thing. The English instead says he does not need someone to worry, reversing the actor and action.
adjudicated.remedy: Use “I couldn’t stop to deal with every little thing.”

adjudicated.jp: 気配はひたひたと追尾してきた。
adjudicated.en: The presence of a pursuit continues steady and gradual.
adjudicated.assessment: The source says the sensed presence steadily follows him. “The presence of a pursuit” turns the pursuer into an abstract property and lacks a clear subject-object relation.
adjudicated.remedy: Use “The presence kept following steadily behind me.”

adjudicated.jp: 腹の虫だ。
adjudicated.en: It's my belly bug.
comments: He talks about everyone being gone, then the eyes, and then he's chased by Youko, and when she leaves the belly bug takes her place. It could be random, but the flow seen here suggests it isn't so. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: 腹の虫 is the idiom for a rumbling stomach or hunger. “Belly bug” translates its components literally and creates a nonexistent creature.
adjudicated.remedy: Use “It was my stomach growling.”
